Project summary
RunAsh AI is an open-source live commerce and streaming platform built on Next.js. It combines live video, chat, AI-assisted workflows, and commerce/payment features for creators, sellers, and platform operators.

Tech stack and runtime
- Runtime: Node.js
- App framework: Next.js App Router (React + TypeScript)
- Styling: Tailwind CSS + PostCSS
- Data and infra integrations: Neon/PostgreSQL, auth providers, cloud storage, realtime and payment-related services
- Package manager lockfile present: pnpm (pnpm-lock.yaml)

Important directories and their intent
- app/: Next.js routes, pages, layouts, API route handlers
- components/: Reusable UI and feature components
- lib/: Core business logic, data access, auth/security utilities, services
- services/: Domain-specific service modules (streaming, speech, platform integrations)
- hooks/: Client-side React hooks
- types/: Shared TypeScript type definitions
- public/: Static assets (images/icons/manifest)
- styles/: Global and theme CSS
- data/: Static JSON/data fixtures

Safe change boundaries
- Safe to edit: feature-specific UI/components, isolated route/page logic, non-breaking utility improvements, documentation updates
- Medium risk (require extra review): auth flows, billing/payment logic, DB access/repositories, realtime/streaming pipelines
- High risk (avoid casual edits): security middleware, secrets handling, production infra configuration, destructive migration/automation scripts

Required validation commands and quality gates
- Install deps: pnpm install
- Lint: pnpm lint
- Build/type gate: pnpm build
- Dev smoke test: pnpm dev (verify critical user flows locally)
- Quality bar: no lint errors, build succeeds, and changed flows are manually sanity-checked before merge

Security rules
- Never expose secrets, tokens, private keys, or raw credentials in code, docs, logs, or commits
- Sanitize logs: avoid PII/session data; redact sensitive identifiers
- Do not add destructive scripts/commands (mass delete, force-reset, unsafe schema/data operations) without explicit maintainer approval
- Prefer least-privilege config changes and keep security-relevant behavior backward compatible unless a reviewed breaking fix is required

Preferred contribution style
- Keep diffs small and scoped to one concern
- Update docs when behavior or features change
- Preserve API compatibility; if a breaking change is unavoidable, document migration steps clearly
